results.caption:
I had 30 days to train for my first IRONMAN (but there was a small catch... I couldn’t swim). Here’s what happened...

Turns out going from zero aquatic talent to a full-distance swim in a month is every bit as chaotic as it sounds 🤣. Throw in a pivot to a swimming pool at 4am, hours of grinding on the bike, and a marathon to close it out, and it’s fair to say the legs felt like they took a 12 round beating from a prime Iron Mikey T.

Huge thanks to @BulldogSkincare for throwing me into the deep end with this challenge and supporting the whole build. The Anytime Daily SPF 50 Moisturiser. was a lifesaver out on the road, and the Original Shower Gel was purely for the safety of everyone around me at the finish line.

Mad day out. Massive respect to every single person taking on these events.

Big love, girls and boys 🫡 

#BulldogSkincare #IRONMANLeeds #IRONMANEurope #ad

results.transcript: I gave myself one month to learn how to swim and cycle, then attempted my first Ironman. Here's my brutally honest review. Swimming? Absolutely horrendous. When Bulldog sent me this challenge, I could barely swim a length. My coach's reaction says it all. So, there's some work to do. Turns out one month isn't enough to turn a flappy Labrador into Michael Phelps. But then, by some divine intervention, the swim got cancelled. And it looked like I might get away scot-free until a leisure centre agreed to open up at 4am so we could get it done anyway. An hour and a half later, everyone had finished. Except me. I had a severe case of maximum inefficiency, but eventually I got it done. Slapped on the Bulldog SPF and made it to the start line for arguably an even harder challenge. 180km on this bad boy. And cycling actually surprised me. Flying down hills at 50km an hour is quite the buzz. My arse, however, in absolute tatters. Seven hours later, I'd made it, which meant finally my bread and bar. A marathon on battered legs. Not fast, not pretty, but after spending all day being terrible at other people's sports, there's no way I wasn't bringing it home from here. In conclusion, swimming. Far too technical. I should have trained longer. Cycling? Surprisingly good fun. Running? Still my numero uno. But the real goat? The hot shower at the end. Overall, bloody good day out. Massive respect for anyone that gets it done. Big thanks to Bulldog for stitching me up with this challenge. The SPF moisturiser has genuinely become a daily essential for me. And the shower gel is even more essential if you've got any respect for anyone that has to be anywhere near you after training. Big love girls and boys.

results.caption: There’s a PLAGUE of “hybrid” athletes coming to endurance sports and completely disregarding all the rules and regulations of the races they enter. This is one of the more ridiculous examples I’ve ever seen. They couldn’t care less about the other runners on the course. So disrespectful and dangerous in my opinion. Share, repost, like, spread this message. 😭 hopefully the right people see this and action is taken. @Sunshine Coast Marathon  !!!

results.transcript: I don't know what it is about hybrid athletes and their need to disrespect the event they go to. This? This is so... I've never seen something so ridiculous. Everything about this is wrong. You got two e-bikes, one e-bike filming the other e-bike offering outside assistance to someone with no bib. Is this guy even in the race? Did he sign up? Apparently, he didn't. Hi, Kyle. You are currently under investigation once again for Marathon Integrity. Initial review indicates you participated in the Sunshine Coast Marathon without an official race entry and collected a finisher's medal and publicly posted it as a registered athlete. So, he's not even in the race. These e-bikes are unofficial e-bikes. This alone should be a ban from the race. There's more. Here's another clip. Same crew. Same race. What? They have like three or four e-bikes out there? Remember, it's an e-bike filming the e-bike. Not only that, they were asked, actually. They were literally asked, instructed by both race officials and police to exit the course on multiple occasions. And they ignored the instructions and returned to the course with their e-bikes. What's the big deal, Coach Noel? Why is this a huge deal? It's a huge deal. It's against the rules. But also, this is super dangerous. And it's so unfair to all the other runners who paid for this race. These races have aid stations. This is for social media. E-bikes are strictly banned for participants and or unauthorized crew. They're not authorized. They just went out there on the course. And then their attitude when confronted was even worse. Thanks for the shout out. We love the exposure. Hi, team. Thanks for the message. Rather than worrying about exposure, we would recommend you do take a level of accountability and think about respecting the event and the other athletes who have paid for the roads to be closed to traffic. Their safety is far more... important than your exposure. I wouldn't have expected a mature response from these people, but boy, they have since turned off their comments, I'm pretty sure. There's this big plague of hybrid athletes who are coming to endurance sports who just don't think the rules apply to them. I know, I'm going to call it out. But this has got to be one of the most egregious, ridiculous, disrespectful displays at an event I've seen in a long time. Not just one e-bike, two e-bikes, filming the other e-bike, breaking the rules. Come on, man. Team Knox, Sunshine Coast. Team Knox. Do better. Oh my gosh.

results.caption:
“Male birth control trial shut down because men couldn’t handle acne.” 🙄 
 The real story is more interesting. 
 Here’s what actually happened:
 📍 The trial ran from 2008 to 2012. 320 men, a hormone injection every 8 weeks.
 📍 It worked. 96% effective — better than condoms.
 📍 The men did NOT quit. An external WHO review panel halted it in 2011, reportedly without consulting the scientists running the study.
 📍 It wasn’t the acne. The panel’s concern was mood — depression, and one suicide attempt.
 📍 And the part nobody posts: over 75% of participants said they’d still use it if it were available. 
 So is there a double standard?  Yes. Just not the one in the memes.
 The pill was approved in 1960, before modern FDA safety rules existed. 
 Women’s mood side effects weren’t taken seriously — they were dismissed for decades.  
 The lesson isn’t “men should tough it out.” It’s that women deserved that same scrutiny, and we didn’t get it. 
 Male birth control is still coming.  
 Share this
 Stay curious about your body 
 Follow me for more ❤️ 📚 References:
 1.	Behre HM, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of an Injectable Combination Hormonal Contraceptive for Men." J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2016;101(12):4779–4788.
 2.	Snopes. "Men Abandoned Male Birth Control Breakthrough Because of Side Effects?" Oct 2016.
 3.	NPR Shots. "Male Birth Control Study Killed After Men Report Side Effects." Nov 2016.
 4.	Skovlund CW, et al. "Association of Hormonal Contraception With Depression." JAMA Psychiatry. 2016.
 5.	STAT News. "As male birth control gets closer to reality, men are lining up for clinical trials." Feb 2026.

results.transcript: But male birth control isn't approved because it can give them tummy aches and pimples. You've seen the post. Male birth control trial shut down because men got acne. I'm a fertility doctor. Let me explain exactly what happened. In 2008 to 2010, a World Health Organization trial gave men a mix of progestion and testosterone every eight weeks to test for a male contraceptive birth control. It worked. 96% effective of shutting down sperm production. In 2011, an outside review panel did shut down the trial, supposedly without asking the scientists first. But it wasn't because of acne. It was because of mood effects, including depression and one suicide attempt. But here's the part no one posts. 75% of men in the trial said they would use this contraceptive method. So is there a double standard? Yes, and not just this one. Number one, the oral contraceptive pill for women was approved in 1960, and the current overhaul and regulatory measures of the FDA did not start until two years later. So it's not that regulators didn't care that women get side effects from birth control pills. It's that they didn't know or have the data. Number two, the FDA has very strict regulations on medications that are considered not medically necessary, and men don't get pregnant. And number three, women's mood side effects from birth control pills ignored and dismissed for decades was finally linked in a 2016 Danish trial. The real scandal? Nobody's funding research into male contraception. No major drug manufacturer is looking into this. The studies are being funded by academics and nonprofits. And the lesson isn't that men should tough it out. It's that women's side effects deserve the same scrutiny. Male birth control? Still coming. There are three trials in the works. I'm Dr. Laura Shaheen. Follow me for more.
